prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: Dino Atlas ecosystem gallery paleoart, brand-new 16:9 landscape scene for ages 5–14
Input images: Image 1 is anatomy-only reference for Scutellosaurus lawleri; Image 2 is anatomy-only reference for Dilophosaurus wetherilli. Preserve only the species identity and body-plan cues described below. Do NOT copy either reference image's composition, pose, camera, backdrop, lighting, color pattern, or object placement.
Primary request: Create a completely new, realistic, non-graphic Early Jurassic Kayenta Formation fauna-context reconstruction with exactly two animals total: exactly one Scutellosaurus lawleri and exactly one Dilophosaurus wetherilli. This illustrates formation-level fauna context in the Kayenta silty facies only; it must not imply the two individuals shared one exact bed or a documented real encounter.
Scene/backdrop: red silty floodplain at the edge of low aeolian dunes, broad dry sediment flats with a few shallow damp patches, sparse period-appropriate ferns, horsetails and low cycad-like plants, and several tall narrow conifer trunks. No modern grass, flowers, mammals, birds, people, buildings, labels, bones, carcasses, or extra animals.
Style/medium: high-quality realistic scientific paleoart, natural surface texture and restrained educational clarity, not a movie poster, not fantasy, not dramatic combat.
Composition/framing: strict 16:9 horizontal landscape; ground-height camera and long telephoto-lens compression; transverse side-view frieze rather than a conventional centered broadside. Tall vertical conifer trunks and plant columns divide the picture into three clearly readable zones. Place the Dilophosaurus near the far-left edge in the middle distance, walking calmly leftward and looking left, with its entire body isolated against open terrain. Place the Scutellosaurus near the far-right edge in the nearer plane, walking calmly rightward while foraging and looking right, with its entire body isolated against open terrain. They face outward away from one another, do not look at each other, and occupy different depth planes. Keep a very broad empty central stretch of red land between them. No chase, attack, stalking, defensive display, contact, overlap, blood, wound, corpse, feeding on animals, or visual eyeline between species. Exactly two animals—no distant silhouettes.
Scale: Dilophosaurus is visibly and unmistakably much larger in actual body size than the very small Scutellosaurus, even though they occupy different depth planes. Do not equalize them.
Scutellosaurus anatomy: very small, slender, lightly built, mostly bipedal herbivore; low small beaked head with no carnivore teeth; exactly two short forelimbs fully visible and separated; exactly two long hindlimbs with both complete feet fully visible and separated; tiny sparse scattered seed-sized oval osteoderms only across back and flanks; one long complete balancing tail visible from pelvis to tip. No large plates, spikes, club, continuous shell, heavy ankylosaur armor, broad quadrupedal body, or four-footed pose.
Dilophosaurus anatomy: much larger bipedal theropod with long low robust skull; exactly two separate parallel nasolacrimal crests, never fused; no neck frill and no venom display; exactly two forelimbs, both fully visible and spatially separated. If hands are readable, each hand has three functional clawed fingers plus one tiny non-clawed peg-like digit IV—never three-only, never four large claws, never five digits, and palms face inward rather than down. Exactly two strong hindlimbs with both complete feet fully visible and separated; one complete long balancing tail visible from pelvis to tip. No single crest, horn, tyrannosaur head or tiny two-finger arms.
Visibility gate: every limb, every foot, each animal's pelvis-to-tip tail, both Dilophosaurus crests, and both species' full silhouettes are entirely inside the frame, unobscured by plants or terrain, non-overlapping and countable. No limb or tail may be cropped by any frame edge. Keep generous breathing room around both animals despite their near-edge placement.
Lighting/mood: clear warm late-afternoon sidelight with gentle cool shadows, calm observational mood, high detail on anatomy, enough depth separation for both animals to remain readable.
Color palette: muted iron-red and rose-brown sediment, dusty sage and deep conifer green vegetation, restrained natural animal colors distinct from the references.
Constraints: exactly 2 animals; full bodies; no text, caption, logo, border, or watermark; no gore; no fantasy anatomy; no motion blur; no foreground plant crossing any limb, foot, head, crest, or tail.
